html:
Retained prompt-macro parsing and integration

The macro package recognizes explicit type-in syntax and selected Parameter Store references. It returns prompt text and context metadata; it does not execute a command or write to a terminal. Its current production integrations include scheduled-event preparation and checks that exclude private inputs from other workflows. It is not a general slash-command interpreter or a universal ordinary composer preprocessing stage.

Scheduler Manager describes the user-facing workflow. Schedule management owns native versus HTTP authority-editing rules. This page explains the retained parser and its actual call boundaries, including compatibility helpers with no production delivery caller in this checkout.

Recognizing literal and macro text

flowchart TD Prompt[Prompt supplied by a parser caller] --> Spoken[Normalize recognized spoken begin/end segments] Spoken --> Mask[Mask quote and Markdown-code positions] Mask --> Token{Unmasked type-in token?} Token -->|No| Sudo{Explicit sensitive sudo value resolves?} Sudo -->|Yes| Payload[Build raw-value context and conditional preview] Sudo -->|No| Store{Recognized use/enter/input field from store?} Store -->|Yes| Parameter[Resolve one parameter value] Store -->|No| Literal[Return text with no macro] Token -->|Yes| Quoted{Quoted input present?} Quoted -->|No| Reference[Resolve explicit key or store query] Reference --> Parameter Quoted -->|Yes| Decode[Decode JSON string and ignore saved placeholders] Decode --> Count{One actual quoted value?} Count -->|None| Literal Count -->|More than one or malformed| Error[Parse error] Count -->|One| Payload Parameter --> Payload Parameter -->|Missing, invalid or ambiguous| Error

syntax_mask.py marks simple single/double quoted spans, inline backticks and triple-backtick fences, including their delimiters. Quoted backslash escapes are tracked; unfinished spans stay masked to the end. Callers check the starting position of a candidate. This is a lexical mask rather than a complete Markdown parser, and it leaves the original text intact.

spoken_controls.py recognizes supported starters such as type in, message and commit description, followed by begin/start and end/stop. It collapses payload whitespace and inserts a JSON-quoted value. Existing quoted/code examples are excluded. Type-in spelling and typo aliases normalize to typein; this helper processes text, not audio.

user_macros.py recognizes case-insensitive typein, type in, tpein and tpe in. A quoted value is a JSON string, so JSON escaping controls quotes and newlines. Missing closing quotes, invalid JSON and multiple actual quoted inputs raise UserMacroParseError. [provided] and [redacted] quoted placeholders are not reparsed as new inputs. Quoted/code examples and slash-prefixed forms such as /typein remain literal. The retained runlater/remind/todo constants do not make those words executable macros in this parser.

The named sanitized_prompt is a normalized representation, not a promise of secret removal. Literal type-in text remains in it; parameter replacement can insert a raw value as a JSON-quoted string. Parsing currently creates redacted=False records. The legacy sensitivity heuristic is not called by this parsing path. Redaction belongs to downstream policy and presentation owners.

Selecting a Parameter Store value

sequenceDiagram participant Parser as Macro parser participant Lookup as Parameter Store participant Select as Scalar field selector participant Result as Prompt/context result alt Explicit key reference Parser->>Lookup: Get named record Lookup-->>Parser: Record or missing/error else Store query Parser->>Lookup: Retrieve bounded original and field-stripped queries opt No candidates collected Parser->>Lookup: Bounded list fallback end Lookup-->>Parser: Unique record identities end loop Candidate records Parser->>Select: Choose requested field or fixed preferred scalar Select-->>Parser: Value/path or incompatible-field error end alt No usable record or requested field Parser-->>Result: Missing-source or field-selection error else Query has multiple compatible records Parser-->>Result: Ambiguity error with candidate keys else One selected record Parser->>Lookup: Record use, best effort Parser->>Result: Raw value, key/path provenance and normalized prompt end Note over Parser,Result: Selection performs no terminal write<br/>and grants no execution permission

Explicit forms can name a key and field, for example typein using password stored in ssh_key. Query forms such as type in ssh password from store gather bounded matches without recording use during discovery. A use/enter/input ... from store phrase without a type-in token must name a recognized field; an ordinary description of a stored service remains literal. Missing stores, missing keys, incompatible values and ambiguous records produce explicit errors rather than selecting an arbitrary record.

The selector walks dictionary keys in sorted order into dotted scalar paths, ignoring lists, nulls and an unkeyed root scalar. A requested field matches the first compatible full path or leaf alias. Without a field, a single scalar is accepted; otherwise the fixed preference order is password, passphrase, token, secret, private key, API key, then value. This priority is deterministic, not an inference about the operator's intent. If no field can be chosen, the error lists available paths.

Query candidate records are deduplicated by normalized key/key. Exactly one scalar-compatible record must remain; multiple records are an ambiguity even when each has a usable password field. Successful selection records usage best-effort; an accounting failure does not undo the selection. Parameter-derived parser macros retain key/field provenance and omit their public preview, while the private payload still contains the value.

Explicit use sudo ... key phrases select only a sensitive named record and produce no macro when lookup or scalar selection fails. The separate prompt_requests_parameter_typein_terminal helper also accepts one exact sensitive retrieval match when the prompt requests credential delivery, excluding explanatory questions. That helper is a terminal-context hint, uses record_use=False, and neither delivers the credential nor changes permissions.

Where production callers use the result

flowchart TD HTTP[Event preparation or<br/>explicit HTTP authority edit] --> Adapter[Prompt/context adapter] Adapter --> Parser[Retained macro parser] Parser -->|Parse failure| BadRequest[HTTP 400 with<br/>safe error text] Parser -->|Actual macro| Context[Normalized prompt and<br/>private/public context lists] Parser -->|No macro| Original[Original adapter prompt<br/>and empty context] Context --> Merge[Merge event context under<br/>existing preservation rules] Original --> Merge Existing[Retained macro context<br/>or pending reference] --> Merge Merge --> Event[Stored scheduled event] Event --> Launch[Occurrence context preparation] Launch --> Hint[Check macro presence<br/>and parameter terminal hint] Hint --> Terminal[Background-terminal owner<br/>handles attachment] Schedule[Prompt scheduling or<br/>authority-preserving edit] --> Exclude[Reject macro-bearing input] Candidate[Execution-cache or<br/>temporal-routing candidate] --> Check[Decline macro dependencies] Parser -.-> Exclude Parser -.-> Check

prompt_context.py translates parse failures to HTTP 400. Actual macros produce shallow-copied context lists and summary event metadata, including a prompt preview that is not redacted here. When no macro remains, this adapter returns the original input prompt rather than the parser's normalized text. Standalone spoken normalization therefore does not automatically become a published prompt change through this adapter.

The parameter-store helper reuses a compatible runtime store or opens the configured database when enabled. Disabled storage becomes unavailable to macro selection. The optional wrapper suppresses HTTP failures; non-HTTP construction failures can still propagate. Compact JSON and SSE helpers serialize supplied payloads without adding redaction.

Event preparation resolves pending macro-context references, strips old macro fields from the base context and prefers newly parsed values. It preserves existing macro context when explicitly requested or when the prompt carries a saved placeholder. Explicit HTTP context/authority editing uses this path. During occurrence preparation, retained macro presence and parameter hints feed the existing background-terminal service. Requesting or attaching a session is separate from delivering an input value.

Other callers use parsing to exclude hidden dependencies:

  • Deterministic prompt scheduling rejects application commands and macro-bearing prompts.
  • Schedule management rejects newly introduced macros when an edit must preserve saved authority.
  • Execution-cache qualification and temporal routing decline inputs with macro dependencies.
  • Terminal escalation treats private macro context or captured type-in requirements as supplied input when deciding whether an input-stripping probe is appropriate.

These integrations do not turn the parser into a general credential broker. Macro metadata and its delivery_scope label do not bypass the owning execution, permission, credential or source-redaction checks.

Retained payload and consumption helpers

sequenceDiagram participant Caller as Explicit helper caller participant Helper as consume_typein_macro participant Context as Caller-owned context dictionary Caller->>Helper: Optional input name, delivery label, action ID, reusable flag Helper->>Context: Find first matching type-in dictionary alt No eligible value or already consumed without reuse Helper-->>Caller: None else Eligible entry Helper->>Context: Mark consumed and append delivery metadata opt Reusable mode Helper->>Context: Increment tolerant delivery counter end Helper-->>Caller: Same mutable macro dictionary end Note over Caller,Context: Bookkeeping only, with no terminal or network I/O<br/>Current use of this helper is in tests

The private-context accessor returns the original dictionary entries so consumption can mutate them; the summary accessor returns shallow copies. Consumption normally skips an already used value. reusable=True permits another record and increments a delivery counter. It does not synchronize threads, write durable state or verify delivery. Repository call-site inspection finds this consumption helper used by tests, with no active production delivery caller.

typein_macro_payloads builds a raw private payload and may include a shortened public preview. Its compatibility redacted argument is currently ignored and the record is constructed with redacted=False. The Parameter Store wrapper delegates to that builder, whereas the parser's parameter path deliberately uses no preview. Do not assume those helper paths have identical presentation behavior.

user_macro_public_delivery formats identity/length and an optional preview; it does not prove delivery. macro_value_with_enter appends a newline when absent and does not send it. These helpers are retained contracts, not evidence of an automatic native terminal-input pipeline.

Verification and limits

Macro tests cover quoted/escaped text, spoken aliases, Parameter Store selection and usage, placeholders, malformed or multiple inputs, terminal hints, in-memory reusable consumption and literal slash commands. All 40 cases pass in isolated fixtures. They neither execute a terminal command nor prove credential delivery. Documentation checks separately compare executable structure and protected literals; the one corrected ordinary helper docstring is permitted only by exact before/after hashes.
